page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9ae.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.25 GHz. Complementing the dedicated CPU cores is 128 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. This configuration addresses computing scenarios where memory capacity is the primary constraint.

Networking performance on the instance is established at a 10 Gbps baseline throughput, supporting distributed network traffic and cluster communication. The ecs.r9ae.4xlarge does not include integrated local storage, requiring persistent data to be hosted on network-attached storage volumes. The instance incorporates no GPU acceleration hardware, focusing resources entirely on CPU and memory tasks. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a resource-efficiency perspective, the 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides a balanced operational profile for memory-heavy services, avoiding the need to overprovision compute cores to attain sufficient RAM. While the absence of onboard NVMe storage necessitates consideration of network storage latency, dedicated compute allocations maintain consistent execution times. The ecs.r9ae.4xlarge is structured for in-memory databases, caching systems, relational database deployments, and enterprise business applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9ae.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz under the KVM hypervisor. The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps and does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, necessitating the use of remote network-attached block storage for persistence. By allocating substantial memory capacity per core, ecs.r9ae.4xlarge offers strong qualitative resource efficiency for applications that prioritize RAM capacity over compute scaling. The architecture is suited for large in-memory caching layers, relational database engines, real-time analytics platforms, enterprise resource planning systems, and transactional enterprise workloads requiring consistent dedicated compute.
